name: with_progress
title: Evaluate an expression with progress handlers

origin.description: Run an expression while progression handlers listen, then shut them down.
origin.usage: with_progress(expr, handlers = progressr::handlers(), cleanup = TRUE, delay_terminal = NULL, delay_stdout = NULL, delay_conditions = NULL, interrupts = getOption("progressr.interrupts", TRUE), interval = NULL, enable = NULL)

arguments.name: expr
arguments.text: An R expression. It is not evaluated until the handlers are active.

arguments.name: handlers
arguments.text: One handler or a list of them. An empty list just evaluates expr.

arguments.name: enable
arguments.text: If FALSE, call the expression and report nothing. In batch mode the default option is FALSE.

arguments.name: cleanup
arguments.text: If TRUE, signal shutdown after the expression, including when it fails.

arguments.name: interrupts
arguments.text: When interrupts are enabled, an interrupt or error asks handlers to interrupt, then the error continues.

origin.details: A reset is signaled before the body. A new initiate shuts down the previous progression when it was not finished. Updates after the progressor has finished warn and are ignored. If any handler target contains terminal, stdout and conditions are delayed and flushed at the end, including messages. The value of the expression is returned.

translation.description: Call a zero-argument function while progression handlers listen, then shut them down.
translation.usage: with_progress(expr, handlers=None, cleanup=True, delay_terminal=None, delay_stdout=None, delay_conditions=None, interrupts=None, interval=None, enable=None)

arguments.name: expr
arguments.text: A zero-argument callable. R delays the expression; Python would evaluate it before the call, so pass a function.

arguments.name: handlers
arguments.text: One handler or a list of them. An empty list just calls expr.

arguments.name: enable
arguments.text: If False, call the function and report nothing. Pass True when stdin is not a terminal, or the handler is a no-op.

arguments.name: cleanup
arguments.text: If True, signal shutdown after the call, including when it raises.

arguments.name: interrupts
arguments.text: If True, an exception of class interrupt or error asks handlers to interrupt. A normal Python exception is the error path. The exception is not swallowed.

translation.details: A control reset is signaled before the body. A new initiate shuts down the previous progression when it was not finished. Updates after the progressor has finished warn and are ignored. If any handler target contains terminal, stdout and message conditions are delayed and flushed at the end. That delay works before a newline handler exists. The callable's return value is returned.
translation.example:
from progressr.condition import condition_message
from progressr.evaluate import with_progress
from progressr.factory import make_progression_handler
from progressr.progressor import progressor

def initiate(config, state, progression, **kwargs):
    print(progression["type"], format(state["step"], "g"))

def update(config, state, progression, **kwargs):
    print(progression["type"], format(state["step"], "g"), condition_message(progression))

handler = make_progression_handler(
    "rec", reporter={"initiate": initiate, "update": update},
    enable=True, target="file", interval=0,
)

def body():
    progress = progressor(along=range(1, 6))
    total = 0
    for value in range(1, 6):
        total += value
        progress(message=str(value))
    return total

print(with_progress(body, handlers=handler, enable=True, interval=0, delay_terminal=False, delay_stdout=False, delay_conditions=()))
